# Pettifer

## Overview

- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v2 c1 P4](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0004)</sub>
- **Origin:** New Brunswick  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Role:** Farmer  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** A crank  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>

## Appearance

Mr. Pettifer resides in a whitewashed, low-eaved, old-fashioned house backed by a thick grove of spruce. He is known to sit on his vine-shaded veranda in his shirt sleeves, enjoying his pipe.

_Sources: [v2 c3 P0](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0000), [v2 c3 P1](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0001)_

## Personality

Regarded locally as an eccentric and stingy crank, Mr. Pettifer is quick-tempered and hasty, yet can be polite, anxious, and gentle once his initial anger passes. He is fiercely independent, maintaining his own home and declaring that he wants no women near his premises. He lacks fixed domestic routines, washing dishes only on rainy Sundays inside a rainwater hogshead and eating only when struck by hunger.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c1 P7](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0007), [v2 c1 P8](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0008), [v2 c3 P1](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0001), [v2 c3 P3](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0003), [v2 c3 P9](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0009)_

## Traits

- Eccentric  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- Stingy  <sub>[v2 c1 P8](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0008)</sub>
- Hasty and quick-tempered  <sub>[v2 c1 P4](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0004), [v2 c3 P1](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0001), [v2 c3 P9](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0009)</sub>

## History

After purchasing Robert Bell's farm to become the western neighbor of Grey Shutters, Mr. Pettifer quickly earned a reputation in Brierley as a stingy eccentric who washed dishes in rain hogsheads and refused to pay minister earnings or mission donations. He hired young John Henry Carter of Pale Sands as his farmhand. When Nell Harcourt mistakenly sold his strayed Jersey cow to a passing dealer, Mr. Pettifer admitted he had acted too hastily previously and gently pardoned her, despite his foul-mouthed parrot Nutmeg repeatedly insulting her. He later employed a clumsy new worker whom he described as having left-handed traits in both feet. When Nell considered writing a fiction story, she confided in Mr. Pettifer, who discouraged her by remarking that too much rubbish was already being published.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c1 P7](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0007), [v2 c1 P8](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0008), [v2 c3 P1](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0001), [v2 c3 P3](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0003), [v2 c3 P8](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0008), [v2 c3 P9](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0009), [v2 c3 P16](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0016), [v3 c11 P50](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0050)_

## Background by volume

- Purchased Robert Bell's farm in Brierley after moving from New Brunswick  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- Received a talking parrot named Nutmeg from his brother, a seafaring man  <sub>[v2 c3 P6](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0006)</sub>
